definitions.explanation: A camera with a single lens system used for both viewing and capturing images, typically with interchangeable lenses. Covers both traditional single-lens reflex (SLR) cameras and modern mirrorless interchangeable-lens cameras.

examples.japanese: {一眼|いちがん}カメラで{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}る。
examples.english: Take photos with a single-lens camera.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めて{一眼|いちがん}カメラを{買|か}ったが、{使|つか}いこなすのが{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: I bought a single-lens camera for the first time, but it's difficult to master.

examples.japanese: {旅行先|りょこうさき}で{一眼|いちがん}カメラを{持|も}ち{歩|ある}くのは{重|おも}いけれど、スマホとは{比|くら}べものにならないほど{綺麗|きれい}な{写真|しゃしん}が{撮|と}れる。
examples.english: Carrying a single-lens camera around while traveling is heavy, but you can take incomparably better photos than with a smartphone.

notes:
Short for {一眼|いちがん}レフカメラ (single-lens reflex camera), though in modern usage it also encompasses mirrorless cameras (ミラーレス{一眼|いちがん}). The term {一眼|いちがん} literally means "one eye" — the single lens is used for both composing and capturing the image, unlike older twin-lens designs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一眼|いちがん}カメラを{買|か}う: to buy a single-lens camera
- {一眼|いちがん}カメラで{撮影|さつえい}する: to shoot with a single-lens camera
- {一眼|いちがん}カメラ{初心者|しょしんしゃ}: single-lens camera beginner
- {一眼|いちがん}カメラ{用|よう}レンズ: lens for single-lens cameras

RELATED WORDS:
- {一眼|いちがん}レフ: SLR (single-lens reflex) — the traditional mirror-based type
- ミラーレス{一眼|いちがん}: mirrorless interchangeable-lens camera
- コンパクトカメラ: compact camera; point-and-shoot
- {望遠|ぼうえん}レンズ: telephoto lens
- {広角|こうかく}レンズ: wide-angle lens
